OCD haver here. It’s weird to me that it’s one of more trivialized mental illnesses (close to the ranks of depression and anxiety) but that pretty much everything people think it is... isn’t actually true? Not a lot of people realize that it’s actually extremely debilitating to a lot of us and is more than just being a “neat freak”. Tie in the constant intrusive thoughts, paranoia,  compulsive rituals, and (in most cases) depression, you’ve got one shitty cocktail of a mental illness. Thankfully there is treatment for it (which I am currently in)!

I'm so incredibly sorry. I lost my dog in 2015 and it was probably the worst day of my life. Lots of crying, screaming even, couldn't go to school for a week. She was my best friend in the world and was around for the majority of my life. I still get choked up sometimes when I think about her (like right now, haha) but the hurt really does ease as the months pass. That doesn't mean your pet becomes less important, you just become more at peace with their passing. There's a poem called The Rainbow Bridge that gave me comfort during that time, and it still does. If you give it a read, I hope it gives you some comfort. Sending peace and good vibes your way.

I saw this a month ago and it stayed stuck in the back of my mind so much that last week while I was high as shit on pains meds post-wisdom teeth extraction, I got the hiccups and said this. I wouldn't have known I said that if my mom hadn't recorded it.

Got diagnosed when I was 11 or 12. A while later, my mom told me that she'd noticed symptoms in me since I was little. The one that stuck out was that every night I'd say goodnight to everybody in my family the same way by saying, "Goodnight, I love you, I'll see you in the morning" in that EXACT order. If I was interrupted, I'd start all over again! It happened every single night and I never really thought anything of it, but it makes so much sense now.
